content:
Doc purpose
- Working notes for the “key ceremony” to create/activate the signing key used to sign Redwood Private offline bundles (air-gapped install artifacts).
- Intended to satisfy internal security requirements + provide evidence trail for SOC2/ISO-style controls.

Background / what this key is for
- Key signs the offline bundle signature envelope (bundle manifest + digests) for Redwood Private on-prem distribution.
- Verification must succeed fully offline; therefore the customer receives public verification material (cert/chain + key id) inside the bundle metadata / or alongside the bundle.
- The signing key MUST be protected (KMS/HSM-backed) and never exported.

In scope for ceremony
- Initial creation + activation of Prod signing key
- Creation of Stage/Test keys for CI integration tests
- Access policy finalization (who/what can sign)
- Audit logging validation (CloudTrail/KMS logs + pipeline logs)
- Rotation schedule + “what happens to old bundles” policy

Out of scope (v1)
- Customer-managed signing keys (customer signs Redwood artifacts) — explicitly not supported in v1.

Proposed key naming conventions
- Prod: kms://redwood-sec/kms/us-east-1/redwood-offline-bundle-signer-prod
- Staging: kms://redwood-sec/kms/us-east-1/redwood-offline-bundle-signer-staging
- CI test: kms://redwood-sec/kms/us-east-1/redwood-offline-bundle-signer-ci-test (restricted; may be allowed to sign only “test” bundle type)

Key type / algorithm (proposal)
- Primary recommendation: asymmetric signing key in HSM-backed KMS (non-exportable).
- Algorithm: ECDSA P-256 (preferred for broad tooling support and small signatures) OR RSA-3072 if customer tooling constraints require.
- Decision needed by Security Eng + Release Eng based on installer verifier library constraints.

Roles & responsibilities (ceremony)
- Executive sponsor / final approver: Dr. Aisha Rahman
- Security Eng owner / ceremony lead: Marcus Lin
- GRC / evidence owner (notes + control mapping): Olga Petrov
- KMS/HSM implementation owner: Hanae Suzuki
- Infra sponsor (KMS/HSM operations + oncall): Neha Kapoor
- Release Engineering owner (CI integration): Connor O’Brien
- Build/CI implementer: Sahana Iyer
- Audit/logging/exports: Kevin Osei
- Incident response / key compromise playbook: Fiona McCarthy
- Product (Security & Compliance) sign-off: Naomi Feldman

Separation of duties (important)
- No single individual should be able to:
  (1) change the release pipeline to invoke signing AND
  (2) modify the KMS key policy to allow that signing AND
  (3) approve the change.
- Proposed split:
  - Release pipeline config changes: Connor/Sahana (Eng)
  - KMS policy changes: Hanae (Sec/Infra) with Marcus review
  - Approval: Aisha + Naomi (policy) and Neha (ops readiness)

Approvals required (before key is used in prod)
1) Threat model reviewed + signed off
- Owner: Marcus
- Approvers: Naomi, Aisha
- Evidence: link to Confluence threat model page + meeting notes

2) Key policy + IAM integration reviewed
- Owner: Hanae
- Reviewers: Marcus, Neha
- Evidence: ticket INT-662, key policy diff, access list

3) Release pipeline signing stage reviewed
- Owner: Connor/Sahana
- Reviewers: Marcus (security), Kevin (logging), Ethan Park (installer integration touchpoint)
- Evidence: GitHub PR link(s), CI logs showing signing + verification, “hermetic/offline” test results

4) Break-glass override policy published
- Owner: Naomi
- Reviewers: Marcus, Olga, Support readiness (Dev Patel)
- Evidence: Confluence policy page + customer acknowledgement language

Ceremony prerequisites checklist
- [ ] INT-662 approved (key request + access policy)
- [ ] Confirm cloud account/project where key lives (prod security account)
- [ ] Confirm HSM-backed KMS tier enabled for that region
- [ ] Confirm CloudTrail/KMS audit logging retention meets requirement (min 1 year; ideally 2+)
- [ ] Confirm “signing service identity” is finalized (CI workload identity / OIDC subject)
- [ ] Confirm CI environment separation (prod signing only in release workflow, not PR workflows)
- [ ] Confirm who has break-glass access to modify key policy (should be very small set)

Ceremony agenda (60–90 min)
1) Review scope and “what this key protects” (Marcus)
2) Confirm algorithm + key spec + region (Hanae)
3) Create key (Hanae shares screen)
4) Apply initial key policy + grants (Hanae; reviewed live by Marcus)
5) Enable key and tag it (see tagging section)
6) Validate audit logs are emitted (Kevin)
7) Dry run: sign a staging bundle in controlled workflow; verify offline in installer (Connor/Ethan)
8) Confirm rotation + revocation approach (Fiona + Marcus)
9) Capture evidence: screenshots/exports + final attendance list (Olga)
10) Action items + next review date (Olga)

Required attendees (minimum)
- Ceremony lead: Marcus
- Key creation operator: Hanae
- Approver: Naomi or Aisha (at least one live; both sign later)
- Audit/logging witness: Kevin
- Release pipeline owner present: Connor or Sahana
- GRC notes: Olga

Key policy requirements (high-level)
- Principle of least privilege:
  - Only the release workflow identity can call Sign/AsymmetricSign on prod key.
  - No human users can sign in steady-state.
- Deny by default to everyone else.
- Explicit restrictions:
  - Scope signing to specific CI workload identity (OIDC subject / service account).
  - Limit to required API actions only (sign + describe key), no schedule deletion/disable by non-break-glass.
- Administrative actions (disable, rotate, change policy) require:
  - Break-glass group membership AND incident/approval ticket.

Tagging requirements (for asset mgmt + audits)
- Environment: prod | staging | test
- System: redwood-private-offline-bundles
- Data classification: security-sensitive
- Owner: security-eng
- Rotation: 180d
- Ticket: INT-662

Audit trail requirements (what we need to be able to show later)
- Who created the key + when (KMS event + change ticket)
- Who approved the key creation and initial policy (email/Slack decision + ticket sign-off)
- Who/what used the key to sign bundles (each signature operation logged)
- Link from every signed bundle back to:
  - release version
  - commit SHA(s)
  - CI build id
  - signer key id / key version
- Evidence location:
  - CloudTrail logs (system of record)
  - CI logs (build/run id)
  - Release manifest metadata (bundle-level)

Access reviews
- Frequency: quarterly review of who can administer the key policy and who can deploy changes to the signing workflow.
- Reviewers: Olga (GRC) + Marcus (Security Eng) + Neha (Infra)
- Evidence:
  - snapshot of IAM groups/roles
  - list of individuals with break-glass permissions
  - sign-off note (this doc or separate quarterly checklist)

Rotation schedule (proposal)
- Prod key rotation: every 180 days (or sooner if required by customer commitments).
- Staging key rotation: every 180–365 days (lower risk but keep practice consistent).
- CI test key: rotate ad hoc; can also be regenerated for test isolation.

How old bundles remain verifiable after rotation
- Verification logic must accept a set of trusted public keys/certs (keyring) shipped with installer/bundle metadata.
- Bundles include signer key id + signature metadata.
- During transition period, installer trusts both old and new keys.
- After deprecation, old key is retained for verification only (do not delete); disable signing usage but preserve ability to validate old signatures if required. NOTE: confirm whether “disable” impacts verification depending on tooling; do not break customer verification.

Revocation / compromise procedure (outline)
- Trigger conditions:
  - suspected unauthorized signing
  - policy tampering
  - CI identity compromise
  - key material compromise (should be extremely unlikely if non-exportable, but include anyway)
- Immediate actions:
  - disable signing permissions (revoke grants / block CI role)
  - freeze releases / quarantine affected bundles
  - incident ticket + exec comms
- Recovery:
  - create new key via emergency ceremony
  - publish updated trusted key set (installer update + out-of-band comms)
  - define how customers should treat bundles signed with compromised key (likely “do not install”; provide list of affected versions)
- Owner: Fiona (IR) + Marcus (Security Eng)

Customer-facing commitments we should be able to state (sanity check)
- Keys are non-exportable and protected by HSM-backed KMS.
- Signing happens only in controlled release pipelines.
- Customers can verify bundles offline using published verification material.
- Rotation occurs on a regular schedule; old bundles remain verifiable.

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Algorithm choice (ECDSA P-256 vs RSA-3072): confirm installer verifier supports both and customer tool expectations.
2) How we distribute trusted verification material:
   - baked into installer binary? shipped as part of bundle? both?
   - update mechanism for new keys in air-gapped environments.
3) Do we need time-stamping for signatures (offline constraints make RFC3161 hard). If not, define how we address “signing time” evidence in audits.
4) Downgrade/replay protections: do we require bundle version monotonicity enforcement in installer?
5) How we label “test signed bundles” so prod installer refuses them (or requires explicit override).

Notes from last sync (12/12)
- Marcus: “Fail-closed by default” means verification failures block install; break-glass requires explicit acknowledgement and structured log.
- Kevin: Need stable fields in logs for export (key id, bundle id, manifest hash, result, override flag).
- Connor: Signing step should run only on release tags, not on main branch merges.
- Hanae: KMS policy should explicitly disallow signing from interactive user sessions.

Action items
- Hanae: draft key policy for prod + staging keys; attach to INT-662 (due 12/20)
- Connor/Sahana: confirm CI workload identity and final signing invocation path (due 12/20)
- Kevin: validate CloudTrail/KMS log retention + export path for audits (due 12/23)
- Olga: create evidence checklist template for ceremony + quarterly access review (due 12/23)
- Fiona: add key compromise section to IR playbook and link from break-glass policy (due 12/27)
